## 【2†In crate std】
# Primitive Type slice [Button: Copy item path]

【337†Read】【338†Write】

1.0.0

Expand description

A dynamically-sized view into a contiguous sequence, `[T]`.

Contiguous here means that elements are laid out so that every element is the same distance from its neighbors.

【339†See also the `std::slice` module】.
Slices are a view into a block of memory represented as a pointer and a length.

    `// slicing a Vec
    let vec = vec![1, 2, 3];
    let int_slice = &vec[..];
    // coercing an array to a slice
    let str_slice: &[&str] = &["one", "two", "three"];`
Slices are either mutable or shared. The shared slice type is `&[T]`, while the mutable slice type is `&mut [T]`, where `T` represents the element type. For example, you can mutate the block of memory that a mutable slice points to:

    `let mut x = [1, 2, 3];
    let x = &mut x[..]; // Take a full slice of `x`.
    x[1] = 7;
    assert_eq!(x, &[1, 7, 3]);`
It is possible to slice empty subranges of slices by using empty ranges (including `slice.len()..slice.len()`):

    `let x = [1, 2, 3];
    let empty = &x[0..0];   // subslice before the first element
    assert_eq!(empty, &[]);
    let empty = &x[..0];    // same as &x[0..0]
    assert_eq!(empty, &[]);
    let empty = &x[1..1];   // empty subslice in the middle
    assert_eq!(empty, &[]);
    let empty = &x[3..3];   // subslice after the last element
    assert_eq!(empty, &[]);
    let empty = &x[3..];    // same as &x[3..3]
    assert_eq!(empty, &[]);`
It is not allowed to use subranges that start with lower bound bigger than `slice.len()`:

【1†ⓘ】

    `let x = vec![1, 2, 3];
    let _ = &x[4..4];`
As slices store the length of the sequence they refer to, they have twice the size of pointers to 【340†`Sized`】 types. Also see the reference on 【341†dynamically sized types】.

    `let pointer_size = size_of::<&u8>();
    assert_eq!(2 * pointer_size, size_of::<&[u8]>());
    assert_eq!(2 * pointer_size, size_of::<*const [u8]>());
    assert_eq!(2 * pointer_size, size_of::<Box<[u8]>>());
    assert_eq!(2 * pointer_size, size_of::<Rc<[u8]>>());`
### 【3†§】Trait Implementations

Some traits are implemented for slices if the element type implements that trait. This includes 【342†`Eq`】, 【343†`Hash`】 and 【344†`Ord`】.
### 【4†§】Iteration

The slices implement `IntoIterator`. The iterator yields references to the slice elements.

    `let numbers: &[i32] = &[0, 1, 2];
    for n in numbers {
        println!("{n} is a number!");
    }`

The mutable slice yields mutable references to the elements:

    `let mut scores: &mut [i32] = &mut [7, 8, 9];
    for score in scores {
        *score += 1;
    }`
This iterator yields mutable references to the slice’s elements, so while the element type of the slice is `i32`, the element type of the iterator is `&mut i32`.

  * 【84†`.iter`】 and 【85†`.iter_mut`】 are the explicit methods to return the default iterators.
  * Further methods that return iterators are 【128†`.split`】, 【153†`.splitn`】, 【51†`.chunks`】, 【173†`.windows`】 and more.
## Implementations【5†§】

### impl<T> 【347†Box】<【348†[T]】>

1.82.0 · 【349†Source】

#### pub fn 【6†new_uninit_slice】(len: 【350†usize】) -> 【347†Box】<[【351†MaybeUninit】<T>]>

Constructs a new boxed slice with uninitialized contents.
##### 【352†§】Examples

    `let mut values = Box::<[u32]>::new_uninit_slice(3);
    // Deferred initialization:
    values[0].write(1);
    values[1].write(2);
    values[2].write(3);
    let values = unsafe { values.assume_init() };

    assert_eq!(*values, [1, 2, 3])`

1.92.0 · 【353†Source】
#### pub fn 【7†new_zeroed_slice】(len: 【350†usize】) -> 【347†Box】<[【351†MaybeUninit】<T>]>

Constructs a new boxed slice with uninitialized contents, with the memory being filled with `0` bytes.

See 【354†`MaybeUninit::zeroed`】 for examples of correct and incorrect usage of this method.

##### 【355†§】Examples

    `let values = Box::<[u32]>::new_zeroed_slice(3);
    let values = unsafe { values.assume_init() };

    assert_eq!(*values, [0, 0, 0])`

【356†Source】
#### pub fn 【8†try_new_uninit_slice】( len: 【350†usize】, ) -> 【357†Result】<【347†Box】<[【351†MaybeUninit】<T>]>, 【358†AllocError】>

🔬This is a nightly-only experimental API. (`allocator_api` 【359†#32838†github.com】)

Constructs a new boxed slice with uninitialized contents. Returns an error if the allocation fails.
##### 【360†§】Examples

    `#![feature(allocator_api)]

    let mut values = Box::<[u32]>::try_new_uninit_slice(3)?;
    // Deferred initialization:
    values[0].write(1);
    values[1].write(2);
    values[2].write(3);
    let values = unsafe { values.assume_init() };

    assert_eq!(*values, [1, 2, 3]);`

【361†Source】
#### pub fn 【9†try_new_zeroed_slice】( len: 【350†usize】, ) -> 【357†Result】<【347†Box】<[【351†MaybeUninit】<T>]>, 【358†AllocError】>

🔬This is a nightly-only experimental API. (`allocator_api` 【359†#32838†github.com】)

Constructs a new boxed slice with uninitialized contents, with the memory being filled with `0` bytes. Returns an error if the allocation fails.

See 【354†`MaybeUninit::zeroed`】 for examples of correct and incorrect usage of this method.
##### 【362†§】Examples

    `#![feature(allocator_api)]

    let values = Box::<[u32]>::try_new_zeroed_slice(3)?;
    let values = unsafe { values.assume_init() };

    assert_eq!(*values, [0, 0, 0]);`

### impl<T, A> 【347†Box】<【348†[T]】, A>

where A: 【365†Allocator】,

【366†Source】
#### pub fn 【10†new_uninit_slice_in】(len: 【350†usize】, alloc: A) -> 【347†Box】<[【351†MaybeUninit】<T>], A>

🔬This is a nightly-only experimental API. (`allocator_api` 【359†#32838†github.com】)

Constructs a new boxed slice with uninitialized contents in the provided allocator.
##### 【367†§】Examples

    `#![feature(allocator_api)]

    use std::alloc::System;

    let mut values = Box::<[u32], _>::new_uninit_slice_in(3, System);
    // Deferred initialization:
    values[0].write(1);
    values[1].write(2);
    values[2].write(3);
    let values = unsafe { values.assume_init() };

    assert_eq!(*values, [1, 2, 3])`

【368†Source】
#### pub fn 【11†new_zeroed_slice_in】(len: 【350†usize】, alloc: A) -> 【347†Box】<[【351†MaybeUninit】<T>], A>

🔬This is a nightly-only experimental API. (`allocator_api` 【359†#32838†github.com】)

Constructs a new boxed slice with uninitialized contents in the provided allocator, with the memory being filled with `0` bytes.

See 【354†`MaybeUninit::zeroed`】 for examples of correct and incorrect usage of this method.
##### 【369†§】Examples

    `#![feature(allocator_api)]

    use std::alloc::System;

    let values = Box::<[u32], _>::new_zeroed_slice_in(3, System);

    assert_eq!(*values, [0, 0, 0])`

【370†Source】
#### pub fn 【12†try_new_uninit_slice_in】( len: 【350†usize】, alloc: A, ) -> 【357†Result】<【347†Box】<[【351†MaybeUninit】<T>], A>, 【358†AllocError】>

🔬This is a nightly-only experimental API. (`allocator_api` 【359†#32838†github.com】)

Constructs a new boxed slice with uninitialized contents in the provided allocator. Returns an error if the allocation fails.
##### 【371†§】Examples

    `#![feature(allocator_api)]

    use std::alloc::System;

    let mut values = Box::<[u32], _>::try_new_uninit_slice_in(3, System)?;
    // Deferred initialization:
    values[0].write(1);
    values[1].write(2);
    values[2].write(3);
    let values = unsafe { values.assume_init() };

    assert_eq!(*values, [1, 2, 3]);`

【372†Source】
#### pub fn 【13†try_new_zeroed_slice_in】( len: 【350†usize】, alloc: A, ) -> 【357†Result】<【347†Box】<[【351†MaybeUninit】<T>], A>, 【358†AllocError】>

🔬This is a nightly-only experimental API. (`allocator_api` 【359†#32838†github.com】)

Constructs a new boxed slice with uninitialized contents in the provided allocator, with the memory being filled with `0` bytes. Returns an error if the allocation fails.

See 【354†`MaybeUninit::zeroed`】 for examples of correct and incorrect usage of this method.
##### 【373†§】Examples

    `#![feature(allocator_api)]

    use std::alloc::System;

    let values = Box::<[u32], _>::try_new_zeroed_slice_in(3, System)?;
    let values = unsafe { values.assume_init() };

    assert_eq!(*values, [0, 0, 0]);`

【374†Source】
#### pub fn 【77†into_array】<const N: 【350†usize】>(self) -> 【357†Result】<【347†Box】<【375†[T; N]】, A>, 【347†Box】<【348†[T]】, A>>

🔬This is a nightly-only experimental API. (`alloc_slice_into_array` 【376†#148082†github.com】)

Converts the boxed slice into a boxed array.

This operation does not reallocate; the underlying array of the slice is simply reinterpreted as an array type.

##### 【377†§】Errors

Returns the original `Box<[T]>` in the `Err` variant if `self.len()` does not equal `N`.
##### 【378†§】Examples

    `#![feature(alloc_slice_into_array)]
    let box_slice: Box<[i32]> = Box::new([1, 2, 3]);

    let box_array: Box<[i32; 3]> = box_slice.into_array().unwrap();`
